summary: Plan faecal sludge services, assess treatment options and map risks. Explore the practical course outline and find the right training for your team.
lede: Faecal sludge management planning helps sanitation planners and engineers assess service areas and plan feasible treatment. It is intended for urban sanitation planners, municipal engineers, utility staff and WASH professionals, and covers mapping service-chain gaps and reviewing sludge characteristics. Learners compare treatment options, estimate indicative capacity needs, identify worker and public-health risks, and organize costs, responsibilities and indicators into a service-area roadmap.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who plan, operate or oversee faecal sludge services, especially where several providers and treatment stages must work together across one urban service area.
audience: Water and Sanitation Utility Operations Staff
prerequisites: Basic familiarity with urban sanitation, onsite sanitation or WASH service delivery is recommended. No coding or specialist software is required.
topics: Water & wastewater treatment and utility management
